gildedrose-console.complexity_measurement_basis: Counted by this pass: 19 decision predicates in UpdateQuality (the for loop, the two comparisons on line 41, and the single predicates on lines 43, 45, 53, 57, 59, 61, 67, 69, 78, 83, 85, 87, 89, 91, 104) + 1. No upstream artifact reported a cyclomatic figure; structural-analysis.json reports only max_nested_conditional_depth_in_update_quality = 5.
gildedrose-console.notes: Entire application: console entry point (Program.cs:8-35), rules engine (Program.cs:37-111), and the Item domain model (Program.cs:115-122) in one file and one namespace. No validation layer, no persistence, no authorization. Rules are interleaved by item type rather than separated, so the method must be read as one unit.
gildedrose-console.reachability: UpdateQuality is a public instance method on the internal class Program and reads the private field Items (Program.cs:5, :7, :37), so the rules engine is unreachable from outside the assembly.

gildedrose-tests.notes: xUnit assembly structurally disconnected from the application: no reference to GildedRose.Console, one test method asserting Assert.True(true) (src/GildedRose.Tests/TestAssemblyTests.cs:10). Every rule in this catalog is unguarded by any test, so all of them are characterization-test candidates before any re-implementation.

rules.name: nightly_inventory_revaluation_sweep
rules.description: One invocation of UpdateQuality revalues the entire inventory exactly once, representing the passage of one business day. It iterates the item list by index and mutates each Item in place; there is no scheduler, no loop over days, no clock read, and no return value. The unit of time is 'one call', not 'one calendar day'.
rules.complexity_rationale: Single counted loop over an IList with no early exit, but it is the orchestration point on which all 24 remaining rules depend, and the order in which it applies them is itself load-bearing (see BR-016).

actions.action: Apply the quality-adjustment phase, then decrement SellIn, then apply the past-sell-by phase, mutating Items[i] in place

An element of Items is null — NullReferenceException at Program.cs:41

rules.name: quality_never_falls_below_zero
rules.description: Quality is never decremented below 0. It therefore holds only because every decrement step is exactly 1 — any future rule that subtracts 2 or more would undershoot the floor undetected.
rules.complexity_rationale: Two identical single-predicate guards; the risk is structural (guard-based rather than clamp-based), not branching complexity.

rules.name: backstage_pass_becomes_worthless_after_the_concert
rules.description: Once SellIn is below 0 a Backstage pass is zeroed. It is written as the self-cancelling expression `Quality = Quality - Quality` rather than an assignment to 0, so any reader searching for a literal zero assignment will miss it. Because this runs after the appreciation phase, the up-to-3 points the pass earned earlier in the same iteration are computed and then thrown away — and the same wasted churn repeats on every subsequent day the pass stays in inventory.
rules.complexity_rationale: Three nested predicates and one assignment; the subtlety is the idiom and the ordering, not the branching.

rules.name: sell_in_means_two_different_things_within_one_iteration
rules.description: The algorithm's correctness depends on an undocumented evaluation order. Quality rules that read SellIn (the Backstage thresholds at lines 59 and 67) execute BEFORE the decrement at line 80, while the expiry test at line 83 executes AFTER it. So within a single iteration 'SellIn' denotes days-remaining-at-start-of-day for the bonus rules and days-remaining-at-end-of-day for the expiry rules. Re-ordering the decrement — the most natural cleanup a developer would make — silently shifts outcomes on the boundary days SellIn 11, 6 and 0, and no test detects it.
rules.complexity_rationale: Not a single branch but an invariant over the whole 75-line method: it spans three phases, five nesting levels and roughly 25 Items[i] accesses, and it is invisible from any one line in isolation. It remains within one module, so it does not meet the extreme threshold of cyclomatic > 30 within a single rule or more than three modules touched.

The SellIn decrement sits textually between the two groups of readers
The expiry test re-reads the already-decremented value

actions.action: The literal thresholds 11 and 6 correctly express '10 days or less' and '5 days or less' only under this ordering; the expiry threshold 0 correctly expresses 'the sell-by date has passed' only under this ordering

rules.name: item_category_is_derived_from_the_exact_display_name
rules.description: There is no category, type or SKU field. An item's entire pricing behaviour is selected by exact, case-sensitive, whole-string equality against three hardcoded display names, at eight comparison sites. Any variation — different casing, a trailing space, a renamed concert, a localised or reworded label — silently reclassifies the item as standard goods with no error. The business taxonomy is therefore coupled to marketing copy.

rules.name: one_run_equals_one_day_with_no_persistence_and_no_idempotence
rules.description: The effective business calendar is the process lifecycle. UpdateQuality is called exactly once per run, there is no clock read, no run-date record and no persistence, so the computed results are discarded at process exit and the next run restarts from the same seed values. Nothing prevents a double run from advancing the inventory two days, and nothing records that a given day was already processed.
rules.complexity_rationale: No branching, but it defines the temporal semantics every other rule is expressed in, and its absence of a run-date guard is the highest-consequence gap for a nightly process.

No output means no way to verify externally that the run did anything at all
boundary_conditions: Zero invocations leave the seed values untouched
There is no upper bound on invocations; SellIn simply keeps falling (see BR-022)

rules.name: interactive_keypress_blocks_unattended_execution
rules.description: After the revaluation, Main calls System.Console.ReadKey() and waits for a human keystroke before exiting. A nightly inventory process therefore cannot complete unattended: in a scheduler or container it blocks indefinitely on a console that will never receive input. This is an operational business rule imposed by a single line.
rules.complexity_rationale: A single statement with no branching, but with a disproportionate operational effect.

conditions.condition: UpdateQuality has returned

actions.action: Block until a key is pressed, then exit; no timeout, no non-interactive fallback, no check for a redirected console

test_hints.happy_path: Run interactively: output "OMGHAI!", then the process waits for a keypress and exits.
error_paths: Run with stdin redirected or under a scheduler: ReadKey throws InvalidOperationException or blocks, depending on host
Run in a container with no console: the process hangs and the scheduled window is missed
boundary_conditions: The revaluation itself has already completed before the block, so the hang does not corrupt the calculation — it only prevents a clean exit code

regulatory_traceability.fidelity_rationale: Operational constraint of a console host; no FAA regulatory source in profiles/faa/compliance.yaml addresses it.

rules.name: sell_in_is_unbounded_below
rules.description: SellIn has no floor and no archival path. It decrements indefinitely on repeated runs, so an item that is 30 days past its sell-by reports SellIn -30. Nothing removes, archives or flags a long-expired item, and there is no int-overflow guard, so the only theoretical limit is int.MinValue.
rules.complexity_rationale: Emergent from an unguarded decrement; no branching of its own.

conditions.condition: Any non-legendary item is processed on any day, including days long after expiry

actions.action: SellIn decrements without limit; only the sign is ever tested, never the magnitude

secondary_sources: src/GildedRose.Console/Program.cs:83 (the only test of the value is SellIn < 0)

test_hints.happy_path: After 20 days a standard item seeded at SellIn 10 reports SellIn -10 with Quality 0.
error_paths: A downstream consumer storing SellIn in a narrower type (tinyint, byte) would overflow where this code does not
boundary_conditions: SellIn 0 → -1 is the only transition with behavioural meaning; every further decrement changes nothing about the rules applied
int.MinValue would wrap on the next decrement — unreachable in practice but unguarded

regulatory_traceability.fidelity_rationale: Numeric range behaviour in a non-regulated domain; no FAA regulatory source in profiles/faa/compliance.yaml addresses it.

rules.name: unknown_or_null_name_is_silently_treated_as_standard_goods
rules.description: The name dispatch has no default-case diagnostic. Because every special-category test is an equality comparison, an item with a null, empty or unrecognised Name falls through to the standard-goods path and quietly depreciates. C# string equality is null-safe, so a null Name does not even raise an exception — it is simply 'not Aged Brie', 'not Backstage passes' and 'not Sulfuras'. Mis-typed or newly introduced merchandise is therefore mispriced without any error, log or warning.
rules.complexity_rationale: Emergent from the absence of an else/default arm; no branching of its own.

conditions.condition: Name is null, empty, or any string not exactly equal to one of the three special literals

actions.action: Apply the standard-goods rules (BR-002, BR-013) with no validation error, log entry or exception

test_hints.happy_path: An item named "Elixir of the Mongoose" — not a special literal — correctly depreciates as standard goods.
error_paths: Name null: no NullReferenceException is raised at the comparisons; the item depreciates silently
Name "": same silent depreciation
boundary_conditions: A null-Name item still has its SellIn decremented at Program.cs:80 and is still subject to double degradation after expiry
Because there is no logging anywhere in the application, a mispriced item leaves no trace

regulatory_traceability.fidelity_rationale: Default-case behaviour in a non-regulated domain; no FAA regulatory source in profiles/faa/compliance.yaml addresses it. SME confirmation is wanted on whether unknown merchandise should depreciate by default or be rejected.

rules.name: inventory_revaluation_is_unauthenticated_and_unaudited
rules.description: There is no authorization rule of any kind: no user, role, permission check, approval step or audit trail governs the revaluation of the entire inventory. The effective rule is that any caller within the assembly may revalue every item, and no record of who changed what is kept. The only access limit is an accidental one — UpdateQuality is public on an internal class and reads a private field, so it is reachable only from inside the assembly.
rules.complexity_rationale: Zero branches; the rule is the documented absence of any access-control or audit logic in the whole application.

conditions.condition: Any in-assembly call to UpdateQuality; no identity, role or permission is consulted

actions.action: Mutate the Quality and SellIn of every item with no approval step, no before/after record and no log entry

test_hints.happy_path: UpdateQuality succeeds with no credential supplied, because none is required.
error_paths: No negative authorization test is possible: there is no code path that can deny the operation
boundary_conditions: Making the class or field more accessible during modernization would widen an unguarded mutation surface
Adding an audit requirement means adding a capability that does not exist today, not modifying one

regulatory_traceability.fidelity_rationale: No FAA regulatory source in profiles/faa/compliance.yaml governs this application's business rules. Note for the compliance line: the absence of AC-3 access enforcement and AU-2/AU-12 audit generation is a NIST 800-53 control-coverage observation handled by the security pass, not a business-rule-to-regulation mapping.

rules.name: conjured_items_degrade_twice_as_fast
rules.description: SPECIFIED BUT NOT IMPLEMENTED. The application's own business documentation requires that "Conjured" items degrade in Quality twice as fast as normal items (README.md:34), and a "Conjured Mana Cake" is seeded into the live inventory at Program.cs:26. But the string "Conjured" appears nowhere in UpdateQuality (Program.cs:37-111) and no branch matches it, so conjured items are currently revalued as ordinary standard goods: -1 per day before the sell-by date and -2 after, instead of the required -2 and -4. The item is being mispriced today, on every run.
rules.complexity_rationale: Implementing it correctly means introducing the first multi-step degradation, which breaks the assumption BR-003 relies on — that every decrement is exactly 1 — so the zero floor must become a clamp rather than a guard, at two sites.

conditions.condition: REQUIRED: item name identifies a Conjured item. No such condition exists in the code — verified by the absence of any "Conjured" comparison in UpdateQuality
ACTUAL: "Conjured Mana Cake" fails every special-name test and falls through to the standard-goods branch

actions.action: REQUIRED: Quality decreases by 2 per day before the sell-by date and by 4 per day after it, floored at 0
ACTUAL: Quality decreases by 1 per day, and by 2 per day after the sell-by date

secondary_sources: src/GildedRose.Console/Program.cs:41-50 (the branch that wrongly claims it)

test_hints.happy_path: Once implemented: "Conjured Mana Cake" at SellIn 3 / Quality 6 should become SellIn 2 / Quality 4.
error_paths: Today the same input yields Quality 5 — the current, incorrect behaviour that a characterization test will lock in unless the gap is resolved first
A naive fix that subtracts 2 without a clamp will drive Quality to -1 from Quality 1, breaking BR-003
boundary_conditions: Quality 1 with a required -2: must land on 0, not -1
Quality 3 expired with a required -4: must land on 0, not -1
Does the rule match by "Conjured" prefix, by substring, or only the exact name "Conjured Mana Cake"? The code gives no answer, and BR-017 shows the codebase has no prefix-matching precedent

regulatory_traceability.requirement_authority: Application business documentation (README.md:34). NOT a regulation: no FAA regulatory source in profiles/faa/compliance.yaml applies to this application, so this is a documentation-to-code gap, not a regulatory compliance gap.
regulatory_traceability.fidelity_rationale: The requirement is stated in the application's own specification and a matching item exists in the live inventory, but no implementing branch exists. Recorded as missing rather than out-of-scope so that no downstream line silently accepts the current behaviour as correct. The business owner must rule on whether this is the intended unfinished state of a refactoring exercise or a live defect.
